answer: One concrete sybil brake is clustered-stake accounting. An agent must first lock a scarce sable bond to a single cold key before any reward turns spendable. When a swarm of new keys suddenly ripple the same vote or attest pattern, the protocol merges them into one cluster and pays that cluster only once. Repeat farms then face a longer vesting spiral with tighter caps, so minting disposable identities costs more than they can extract, while a lone honest agent keeps a full share.
